preamble: Retroflexion of the palato-alveolar ejective affricate [tʃʼ] to the retroflex ejective [ʈʂʼ] in the Mamean languages (Mam, Tektitek, Awakatek, Ixil) and in Qʼanjobʼal, Akatek and Poptiʼ. In Kaufman & Justeson's (2003) Preliminary Mayan Etymological Dictionary, cognate sets reconstructed with *ch' have ch' in Kʼicheʼ, Chuj, Tojolabʼal and Mochoʼ but tx' in these languages: Proto-Mayan *ch'aj 'wash' is Poptiʼ tx'ah, Awakatek tx'aj and Ixil tx'a beside Kʼicheʼ and Mochoʼ ch'aj, and *ch'o7h 'rat, mouse' is Qʼanjobʼal and Poptiʼ tx'ow beside Chuj ch'o7w. Forms are cited in the dictionary's spelling, in which 7 is the glottal stop. In the ALMG convention for these languages ch' is [tʃʼ] and tx' is [tʂʼ] (Wikipedia, Mayan languages), and Wikipedia's Mam, Qʼanjobʼal and Ixil articles list txʼ as [ʈ͡ʂʼ]. Wikipedia's Proto-Mayan article, citing Campbell (1997: 164), describes a Mamean chain shift *r > t, *t > tʃ, *tʃ > tʂ, *ʃ > ʂ and says the retroflex affricates and fricatives later diffused into Qʼanjobʼalan. It names only the plain affricate; the ejective here rests on Kaufman & Justeson's cognate sets. In the same sets Chuj, Tojolabʼal and Mochoʼ keep ch'. Not every set has tx' throughout: Awakatek has ch'ooy 'ratón' in the *ch'o7h set and Ixil has ch'ach 'cama' in the *ch'aht set, where the neighbouring languages have tx'.
